synopsis: ISO/PAS 34506 concerns qualification of virtual test environments for road vehicles; it remained a draft in October 2026 and should not be treated as a finished standard [f4334, f7695, f15318]. The glossary also distinguishes its Publicly Available Specification status from a full standard [f15052]. Alongside ISO 34502–34505, it offers methodological precedent for structuring site, weather and behavior combinations for off-road automatic braking, with scenario coverage required to reflect the operational design domain, but provides no off-road compliance evidence [f8123, f8121, f15320]. The corpus identifies no demonstrated validity for mines, quarries, earthworks or challenging heavy-machine conditions, and says these frameworks focus on coverage rather than validation against physical data [f7696, f8120]. They also neither address risk scaling nor establish a physical-to-virtual testing ratio, leaving those evidence-planning questions unresolved [f8119, f8122, f15321].
